extracted.intended_audience: parties and practitioners participating in FCC adjudicatory and notice-and-comment rulemaking proceedings (petitioners, commenters, licensees, counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements governing affirmative, responsive, and reply case submissions in hearings, and procedures for petitions, notices, comments, replies, and petitions for reconsideration in FCC notice-and-comment rulemaking proceedings under 5 U.S.C. 553.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative case submission required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The affirmative case submission shall include: (1) A statement of relevant material facts, supported by sworn statements based on personal knowledge, documentation, or by other materials subject to consideration by the presiding officer, and a full legal analysis of each of the issues designated for hearing; (2) Citation to relevant sections of the Communications Act or Commission regulations or orders; and (3) The relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmative case must 'fully address each of the issues designated for hearing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative case must address designated factual and legal questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The affirmative case submission shall address all factual and legal questions designated for hearing, and state in detail the basis for the response to each such question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses based on information and belief are prohibited unless made in good faith and accompanied by a declaration or affidavit explaining basis and why facts could not reasonably be ascertained. If denying only part of a designated question, specify true portions and deny only the remainder. Failure to address all designated questions may result in adverse inferences against the filing party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsive case submission required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsive case submission shall include: (1) A statement of relevant material facts, supported by sworn statements based on personal knowledge, documentation, or other materials subject to consideration by the presiding officer, and a full legal analysis of any issues designated for hearing; (2) Citation to relevant sections of the Communications Act or Commission regulations or orders; and (3) Any relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsive case must be filed within 30 calendar days of the affirmative case submission unless otherwise directed. It should specifically respond to all material allegations made in the affirmative case and attempt to narrow issues for the presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements deemed admitted if not rebutted
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of fact or law in an affirmative case filed pursuant to § 1.372 are deemed admitted when not rebutted in a responsive case submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should rebut material allegations to avoid admission by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply case submission required elements and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply case submission shall contain statements of relevant material facts, supported by sworn statements based on personal knowledge, documentation, or other materials subject to consideration, and a full legal analysis that responds only to the factual allegations and legal arguments made in any responsive case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply cases must be filed within 15 days of a responsive case submission unless otherwise directed. Other allegations or arguments outside the responsive case will not be considered. Failure to submit a reply is not deemed an admission of allegations in the responsive case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other written submissions and presiding officer authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may require or permit parties to file other written submissions such as briefs, proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law, or other supplementary documents or pleadings, and may limit the scope of such pleadings to certain subjects or issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer may also require additional information deemed appropriate for a full, fair, and expeditious resolution of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion and standards to request an oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file a motion to request an oral hearing after submission of all pleadings but no later than the date established in the scheduling order. The motion shall contain a list of genuine disputes as to outcome-determinative facts that the movant contends cannot adequately be resolved on a written record and a list of witnesses whose live testimony would be required to resolve such disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motion must contain supporting legal analysis including citations to relevant authorities and parts of the record. If the presiding officer finds a genuine dispute as to an outcome-determinative fact that cannot be resolved on the written record, an oral hearing limited to necessary testimony and cross-examination will be conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer authority to initiate oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may, on his or her own motion following receipt of all written submissions, conduct an oral hearing to resolve a genuine dispute as to an outcome-determinative fact that cannot adequately be resolved on a written record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any oral hearing conducted by the presiding officer shall be limited to testimony and cross-examination necessary to resolve that dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument permitted only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral argument shall be permitted only if the presiding officer determines that oral argument is necessary to resolution of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should not assume oral argument will be granted; show necessity where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of written hearing record
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission is the presiding officer and it has appointed a case manager under § 1.242, the case manager shall certify the record for decision to the Commission promptly after the hearing record is closed, and notice of such certification shall be served on all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart C (applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart shall be applicable to notice and comment rulemakings proceedings conducted under 5 U.S.C. 553, and shall have no application to formal rulemaking (or rate making) proceedings unless the Commission directs otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'party' in this subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: As used in this subpart, the term 'party' refers to any person who participates in a proceeding by the timely filing of a petition for rule making, comments on a notice of proposed rule making, a petition for reconsideration, or responsive pleadings in the manner prescribed by this subpart. The term does not include those who submit letters, telegrams or other informal materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may petition for rulemaking and petition content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may petition for the issuance, amendment or repeal of a rule or regulation. The petition shall conform to the requirements of §§ 1.49, 1.52, and 1.419(b) (or § 1.420(e), if applicable), and shall set forth the text or substance of the proposed rule, amendment, or rule to be repealed, together with all facts, views, arguments and data deemed to support the action requested, and shall indicate how the interests of petitioner will be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions to amend FM/TV tables must be served on affected licensees/permitees and accompanied by certificate of service; petitions which are moot, premature, repetitive, frivolous, or plainly do not warrant consideration may be denied or dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and availability of petitions for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: All petitions for rulemaking meeting the requirements of § 1.401 will be given a file number and, promptly thereafter, a 'Public Notice' will be issued describing the petition, file number, nature of the proposal, and date of filing. Petitions are available through the FCC Reference Information Center and may be available electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses to petitions — timing and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may file a statement in support of or in opposition to a petition for rule making prior to Commission action on the petition but not later than 30 days after 'Public Notice' is given. Such a statement shall be accompanied by proof of service upon the petitioner and shall conform with the requirements of §§ 1.49, 1.52, and 1.419(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies to such statements may be filed prior to Commission action but not later than 15 days after filing of such a statement. No additional pleadings may be filed unless specifically requested by the Commission or authorized by it. Statements and replies shall not be filed after Commission action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission action on petitions (institution, notice, denial)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission determines that the petition discloses sufficient reasons to justify institution of a rulemaking proceeding and notice and public procedure are required or desirable, an appropriate notice of proposed rule making will be issued. Where notice and public procedure are not required, the Commission may issue a final order amending the rules. In all other cases the petition will be denied and the petitioner notified of the Commission's action with the grounds therefor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed rulemaking — ordinary methods and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice is ordinarily given by publication of a 'Notice of Proposed Rule Making' in the Federal Register (a summary of full decision constitutes notice). If all persons subject to the proposed rules are named, the proposal may be personally served upon those persons. If all persons are named and have actual notice as a matter of law, further prior notice is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule changes relating to military/foreign affairs, Commission management/personnel, interpretative rules, general statements of policy, or rules of Commission organization/procedure/practice will ordinarily be adopted without prior notice. Commission may adopt without prior notice where it finds good cause and must publish the finding and basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of the proposed issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule will include: (a) A statement of the time, nature and place of any public rulemaking proceeding to be held; (b) Reference to the authority under which the issuance, amendment or repeal is proposed; (c) Either the terms or substance of the proposed rule or a description of the subjects and issues involved; (d) The docket number assigned to the proceeding; and (e) A statement of the time for filing comments and replies thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to submit comments and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice of proposed rulemaking is issued, the Commission will afford interested persons an opportunity to participate in the rulemaking proceeding through submission of written data, views, or arguments, with or without opportunity to present the same orally in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reasonable time will be provided for submission of comments and replies (specified in notice). No additional comments may be filed unless specifically requested or authorized by the Commission. In some proceedings, ex parte communications with Commission staff may be permitted under specified procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and number of copies for comments and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments, replies, and other documents filed in a rulemaking proceeding shall conform to the requirements of § 1.49. Unless otherwise specified, an original and one copy of all comments, briefs and other documents shall be furnished to the Commission (total 2). Participants who wish each Commissioner to have a personal copy may file an additional 5 copies (total 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the general public may submit an original and one copy informal comment without regard to form provided the docket number is specified. Participants filing identical documents in more than one docket must furnish two additional copies for each additional docket. Electronic filers need submit only one copy if conforming to electronic filing requirements. Electronic filings by parties represented by an attorney must include the name and mailing address of at least one attorney; unrepresented filers must provide name and mailing address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures for amendments to FM/TV Tables of Allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments filed in proceedings for amendment of FM or Television Tables of Allotments initiated on a petition for rule making shall be served on petitioner. Reply comments shall be served on those who filed the comments to which the reply is directed. Such comments and reply comments shall be accompanied by a certificate of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterproposals shall be advanced in initial comments only and will not be considered if advanced in reply comments. An original and 4 copies of all petitions for rulemaking, comments, reply comments, and other pleadings shall be filed with the Commission (unless otherwise specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certificate requirements for certain pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for reconsideration and responsive pleadings shall be served on parties to the proceeding and on any licensee or permittee whose authorization may be modified to specify operation on a different channel, and shall be accompanied by a certificate of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may modify licenses in rulemaking under specified conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may modify the license or permit of a UHF TV station to a VHF channel or modify an FM station to another class of channel through notice and comment procedures if specified conditions are met (e.g., no other timely filed expression of interest; or if another interest timely filed, an additional equivalent class also allotted/available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some cases Commission may modify license to specify a new community of license where amended allotment would be mutually exclusive. Note: certain station upgrade requests that would overlap a TV station's contour must meet a particularly heavy burden demonstrated to be in the public interest; Commission will examine record to determine availability of non-commercial educational service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit and disclosure requirements for dismissal/withdrawal of expressions of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: When an expression of interest in applying for, constructing, and operating a station has been filed and the filing party seeks to dismiss or withdraw the expression of interest (unilaterally or in exchange for consideration), that party must file a request for approval, a copy of any written agreement related to the dismissal/withdrawal, and an affidavit setting forth: (1) Certification that neither the party withdrawing nor its principals has received or will receive money or other consideration in excess of legitimate and prudent expenses; (2) Exact nature and amount of any consideration received or promised; (3) Itemized accounting of expenses for which it seeks reimbursement; (4) Terms of any oral agreement related to the dismissal or withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 5 days of a party's request for approval each remaining party to any written or oral agreement must submit an affidavit certifying it has not paid or will not pay consideration in excess of legitimate expenses and stating terms of any oral agreement relating to dismissal/withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further notice of rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: In any rulemaking proceeding where the Commission deems it warranted, a further notice of proposed rulemaking will be issued with opportunity for parties of record and other interested persons to submit comments in conformity with §§ 1.415 and 1.419.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument and other proceedings notice
rubrics_metrics.description: In any rulemaking where the Commission determines that an oral argument, hearing or any other type of proceeding is warranted, notice of the time, place and nature of such proceeding will be published in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission consideration of comments and issuance of decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will consider all relevant comments and material of record before taking final action in a rulemaking proceeding and will issue a decision incorporating its finding and a brief statement of the reasons therefor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of rules — general 30-day requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any rule issued by the Commission will be made effective not less than 30 days from the time it is published in the Federal Register unless otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the report and order does not specify the effective date, the effective date shall be 30 days after publication unless a later date is required by statute or specified by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to 30-day effective date requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For good cause found and published with the rule, any rule may be made effective in less than 30 days. Rules involving military/foreign affairs, Commission management/personnel, public property/loans/grants/benefits/contracts, rules granting/recoognizing exemptions or relieving restriction, rules of organization/procedure/practice, interpretative rules, and statements of policy may be made effective without regard to the 30-day requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of good cause and basis must be published with rule changes adopted without prior notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longer notice for alterations in carriers' accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases of alterations by the Commission in the required manner or form of keeping accounts by carriers, notice will be served upon affected carriers not less than 6 months prior to the effective date of such alterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reconsideration — who may file and filing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may petition for reconsideration of a final action in a proceeding conducted under this subpart. The petition for reconsideration shall be filed within 30 days from the date of public notice of such action, shall not exceed 25 double-spaced typewritten pages, and shall state with particularity the respects in which petitioner believes the action taken should be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where action was taken by the Commission the petition will be acted on by the Commission; where action was taken by a staff official the petition may be acted on by staff or referred to Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for granting petitions relying on new facts or arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for reconsideration which relies on facts or arguments not previously presented will be granted only if: (1) The facts/arguments relate to events/circumstances occurring since the last opportunity to present them; (2) They were unknown to petitioner until after the last opportunity and could not with ordinary diligence have been discovered earlier; or (3) The Commission determines that consideration is required in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements and page limits for oppositions and replies to petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions to a petition for reconsideration shall be filed within 15 days after public notice of the petition's filing and shall not exceed 25 double-spaced typewritten pages. Replies to an opposition shall be filed within 10 days after the time for filing oppositions has expired and shall not exceed 10 double-spaced typewritten pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions, oppositions and replies shall conform to §§ 1.49 and 1.52, except that petitions need not be verified. Except as provided in § 1.420(e), an original and 11 copies shall be submitted to the Secretary; electronic submissions by parties filing in electronic form need only submit one copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing a petition for reconsideration on judicial review and rule enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a petition for reconsideration is not a condition precedent to judicial review of any action taken by the Commission, except where the person seeking review was not a party to the proceeding or relies on questions of fact or law upon which the Commission had no opportunity to pass. The filing of a petition does not excuse compliance with any rule or stay enforcement absent good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission may stay effective date pending decision on petition upon good cause shown; petitions that plainly do not warrant consideration may be dismissed or denied by relevant bureaus/offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of petitions for reconsideration that may be dismissed
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions may be dismissed or denied if they: (1) Fail to identify any material error, omission, or reason warranting reconsideration; (2) Rely on facts/arguments not previously presented that do not meet the new-facts standards; (3) Rely on arguments fully considered and rejected in the same proceeding; (4) Fail to state with particularity the respects in which action should be changed; (5) Relate to matters outside the scope of the order; (6) Omit information required to be included; (7) Fail to comply with procedural requirements; (8) Relate to an order for which reconsideration was previously denied on similar grounds (with limited exceptions); or (9) Are untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of rulemaking provisions to Notices of Inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this subpart also govern proceedings commenced by issuing a 'Notice of Inquiry,' except that such proceedings do not result in the adoption of rules, and Notices of Inquiry are not required to be published in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show cause order content and carrier response requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An order to show cause shall contain a statement of the particulars and matters concerning which the Commission is inquiring and the reasons for such action, and will call upon the carrier to appear and give evidence upon the matters specified. Any carrier served shall file its answer within the time specified and shall specifically and completely respond to all allegations and matters contained in the show cause order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All papers filed by a carrier in such proceedings must conform with §§ 1.49 and 1.50 and the subscription and verification requirements of § 1.52.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearances for hearings and oral arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise required in specified sections or by Commission order, no written statement indicating intent to appear need be filed in advance of actual appearance at any hearing by any person or his attorney. For oral arguments, within 5 days after release of an order designating an initial decision for oral argument any party who wishes to participate shall file a written statement indicating they will appear and setting forth reasons for their interest. The Commission will advise whether the party may participate. The requirement does not apply to counsel representing the Commission or Chief of the Enforcement Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file required appearance statements in proceedings involving oral arguments may result in penalties as provided in § 1.277.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal complaint form content
rubrics_metrics.description: An informal complaint shall be in writing and should contain: (a) The name, address and telephone number of the complainant; (b) the name of the carrier against which the complaint is made; (c) a complete statement of the facts tending to show that such carrier did or omitted to do anything in contravention of the Communications Act; and (d) the specific relief or satisfaction sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal complaint procedure and forwarding to carrier
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will forward informal complaints to the appropriate carrier for investigation and may set a due date for the carrier to provide a written response to the informal complaint to the Commission, with a copy to the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the carrier's response or other communications indicate the complaint has been satisfied, the Commission may consider the proceeding closed. If not satisfied or no response by due date, the complainant may file a formal complaint in accordance with § 1.721.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation-back of formal complaints to informal complaint filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: When an informal complaint has not been satisfied, the complainant may file a formal complaint in the form specified in § 1.721. Such filing will be deemed to relate back to the filing date of the informal complaint provided the formal complaint is filed within 6 months from the date of the carrier's response (or due date if no response), references the date of the informal complaint, and is based on the same cause of action as the informal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no formal complaint is filed within the 6-month period the informal complaint proceeding will be closed.
